title: BRICKSTORM Backdoor Investigation
description: Investigate the BRICKSTORM backdoor, a sophisticated 64-bit ELF executable written in Go, targeting Linux systems. It employs advanced evasion techniques such as SOCKS proxying, multi-layered web service communication, and varied command execution.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Unix/Linux system administration
Basic networking knowledge with an emphasis on Linux-based systems
Familiarity with systemd and service management
outcomes: Identifying suspicious services on Linux systems
Analyzing network connections for C2 communication

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The BRICKSTORM backdoor is a sophisticated 64-bit ELF executable written in Go, targeting Linux systems. It employs advanced evasion techniques such as SOCKS proxying, multi-layered web service communication, and varied command execution. The backdoor uses Domain over HTTPS (DoH), nested TLS encryption, and abuses legitimate cloud services to evade detection. It is capable of C2 communication, lateral movement, data exfiltration, and persistence. This scenario will guide you through investigating a compromised system exhibiting BRICKSTORM backdoor behaviors.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host `target` (IP: 192.168.50.5) using SSH with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`.
levels.local_content: Access the target host `target` (IP: 192.168.50.5) using SSH with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`.

levels.title: Identify the Suspicious Service
levels.content: Investigate the services running on the target host and identify the suspicious service name flag related to the BRICKSTORM backdoor. You are looking for a service name flag.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or unfamiliar services. The suspicious service name flag is `updatemgr.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd services can be listed using specific commands. Look for services that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and examine their names.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The suspicious service name flag starts with 'updatemgr'. Look for any service that matches this pattern.

levels.title: Investigate the Suspicious Outbound IP and Port
levels.content: Analyze the network connections on the target host to identify any suspicious outbound IP addresses and ports used by the BRICKSTORM backdoor for C2 communication. You are looking for an IP:port flag.
levels.solution: Use tools like `netstat`, `ss`, or `tcpdump` to inspect network connections. The suspicious outbound IP and port flag is `192.168.40.5:443`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Network connections can be inspected using various tools. Focus on outbound connections that seem unusual.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `netstat -tuln` to list all network connections and look for suspicious outbound IPs and ports.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The suspicious outbound IP and port flag is `192.168.40.5:443`. Look for this specific pattern in the network connections.

levels.title: Identify the File Transfer Mechanism for Lateral Movement
levels.content: Investigate the file transfer mechanism used by the BRICKSTORM backdoor for lateral movement between the target and next-target hosts. You are looking for a service name flag.
levels.solution: Examine the system logs and processes to identify the service responsible for transferring files between the hosts. The file transfer mechanism service name flag is `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: File transfer mechanisms often involve specific services. Look for services that might be responsible for transferring files.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and look for any that might be involved in file transfer.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The file transfer mechanism service name flag starts with 'payload-transfer'. Look for any service that matches this pattern.
